lines: מִי כָמוֹךָ נִרְאֶה בְּתוֹךְ כִּבְשַׁן אֵשׁ

review: The printed grid is 2/4/4/4: stanza 1 is the refrain doubled, stanza 2 reopens with the same refrain and then lists three wonders, stanzas 3–4 run the long lines. The payload keeps that grid so the refrain opens stanzas 1 and 2 exactly where the Arabic prints لَمْ تَرَ عَيْنٌ إِلٰهًا غَيْرَكَ.

1:1 עַיִן לֹא־רָאֲתָה — 1 Cor 2:9 (עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה, Isa 64:3); the Arabic is that verse put as a confession, and the Hebrew keeps the eye and the 'not seen' rather than a general negative then the two other senses, because only eye is in the line.

2:2–2:3 פּוֹתֵחַ סֹהַר … בּוֹקֵעַ מְצוּלָה — Isa 42:7 (מִמַּסְגֵּר אַסִּיר) and Exod 14:21 (וַיִּבָּקְעוּ הַמָּיִם); סֹהַר is the prison of Gen 39:20 and מְצוּלָה the deep of Ps 69:3, kept as two distinct nouns so 'prison' and 'depths' do not collapse into one.

3:1–3:2 are the three men in the furnace (Dan 3) and Daniel in the den (Dan 6:17, גֹּב אַרְיָוָתָא); the Hebrew uses בּוֹר ('pit') as the Arabic uses جُبّ, and keeps מִי ('who?') as the anaphora of all four lines so the stanza stays a chain of wonder-questions.

4:1–4:2 כַּמָּה עֻנֵּיתָ — the Arabic كَمْ تَأَلَّمْتَ is 'how You suffered'; the Hebrew keeps the 'how many/how much' question and the passive-suffering verb, because the stanza's point is the measure of the passion, not merely that it happened.

The refrain line is pointed fully and is ten syllables by the checker; the surrounding lines are the long hexametric wonders, so this hymn is among those where the printed metre (11.11.11.11 – 11.11) only loosely governs and the refrain is set apart by design.
